answer: Sequential Effort Chain. Each identity must publish a chain of small, verifiable compute tasks, one completing at dawn each day. A new identity joins only by extending an existing thread backward: its first task must reference and validate the prior day's output of a sponsor chain. Hollow claims break because validation requires reproducing the exact intermediate state. Attacker cost: one full day of sequential compute per identity plus re-deriving the sponsor's history, so mass registration scales linearly in wall-clock time, not parallel capital.
